mexico.text: Home to the oldest wine-growing region in the Americas, planted by the Spanish in the 16th century. Baja California makes 90% of the wine, and the most planted grapes include Sultaniye, Cabernet Sauvignon, Carignan and Merlot.

mexico/baja-california.text: A Mexican wine region that makes about 90% of the country's wine. Its Ruta del Vino links over fifty wineries with the port of Ensenada and the border, and it is promoted for wine tourism.

mexico/coahuila.text: A Mexican wine region that includes the Valle de Parras. Parras is where a Cabernet Sauvignon won the trophy for the world's best Cabernet at the 2020 International Cabernet competition.

mexico/valle-de-parras.text: A valley in Coahuila, Mexico. A Parras Cabernet Sauvignon, Don Leo Gran Reserva, won the trophy for the world's best Cabernet at the 2020 International Cabernet competition.

mexico/valle-de-guadalupe.text: A valley in Baja California, the state that makes about 90% of Mexico's wine. It holds smaller valleys including Calafia, Mexicali, San Vicente, Santo Tomás and the Tecate zone.

netherlands.text: A small wine producer that is a strong and growing branch of Dutch farming, with 180 commercial vineyards. Chardonnay is the most planted grape, followed by Pinot Noir and the hybrid Johanniter.

netherlands/achterhoek-winterswijk.text: A Dutch PDO around the commune of Winterswijk. It allows still, semi-sparkling, sparkling and liqueur wines, plus wines from raisined or overripe grapes. Allowed grapes include Solaris, Johanniter, Regent and Souvignier Gris.

netherlands/maasvallei-limburg.text: A Dutch PDO for still wine along the Maas valley in Limburg. Allowed grapes include Riesling, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris, Auxerrois and Gewürztraminer, plus Acolon and Dornfelder for reds.

netherlands/mergelland.text: A Dutch PDO for still and sparkling wine around Maastricht, Valkenburg and Vaals. Allowed grapes include Riesling, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Pinot Blanc, Pinot Gris, Auxerrois and Müller-Thurgau.

netherlands/oolde.text: A Dutch PDO in the commune of Lochem. It allows still, semi-sparkling, sparkling and liqueur wines, and wines from overripe grapes. Allowed grapes include Solaris, Regent, Cabernet Blanc, Cabertin and Pinotin.

netherlands/vijlen.text: A Dutch PDO in the commune of Vaals, allowing still and sparkling wine. Allowed grapes include Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Pinot Gris, along with Solaris, Muscaris, Johanniter and Cabernet Cortis.

netherlands/rivierenland.text: A Dutch PDO since 2022 for wine from along the Rhine, Waal, Linge and Oude IJssel rivers in Gelderland. It sits on a river floodplain of sandy, clay and gravelly layers, with fertile soils suited to vines.

netherlands/pgis.text: The group of twelve Dutch PGIs, one for each province: Zeeland, Zuid-Holland, Utrecht, Overijssel, Noord-Holland, Noord-Brabant, Limburg, Groningen, Gelderland, Friesland, Flevoland and Drenthe.

turkey.text: A country where grape growing in Anatolia goes back at least 7,000 years, and one of the first places Vitis vinifera was domesticated. It has the world's sixth-largest vineyard area, but only 3% to 15% of the harvest becomes wine. Sultaniye, Öküzgözü, Syrah and Boğazkere lead plantings.
